charter: v2

# ADR-034 — Avatar renderer (Rive Renderer vs Flutter/Impeller replay) (P11-032)

Status: **Accepted** (Tope, 2026-10-27). Implements ELEVATION §4.2 L911 and §4.5–§4.6 frame budgets.

## Context

`lingafriq_cast.riv` (ADR-030 CharacterVM, ADR-033 lip-sync timings) must render on 2020 mid-range Android (Tecno/Infinix class) at **≤ 2 ms/frame** avatar cost and **60 fps** target (graceful **30 fps** when thermally throttled).

Two rendering strategies were compared:

| Strategy | Description | Fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A — Rive Renderer** | `rive ^0.14.11` + `rive_native`; Rive Renderer draws the artboard; Flutter **Impeller** composites the `RiveWidget` layer only | Matches §4.5; one `.riv` source; GPU vector path |
| **B — Flutter/Impeller replay** | Re-draw L1–L5 layers with Flutter `CustomPainter` / Impeller scene graph, no Rive draw path | Rejected: duplicates art pipeline, breaks VM contract tests, draw-call budget untenable |

Impeller remains the **Flutter engine renderer** in all cases; the decision is whether avatar pixels come from **Rive Renderer (A)** or a bespoke Impeller replay (B).

## Measurement (2 ms/frame budget)

**Metric:** `t_avatar = t_advance + t_render` for artboard `Character`, preset `Polie`, activity `celebrating`, 200×200 logical px, 600 consecutive frames at 60 Hz target.

**Source artefact:** `assets/rive/lingafriq/AVATAR_DIRECTOR_INTEGRATION.md` §5 (Rive CLI against `lingafriq_cast.riv`, v3.2 file **298,228 B** ≤ 300 KB).

| Component | Environment | Mean (ms) | p95 (ms) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `t_advance` (state machine + VM) | CLI bench, 600 frames | **0.147** | **0.18** | Production path always pays this |
| `t_render` (Rive draw) | CLI, **software GL** | 4.2 | — | **Disqualified** — not used on device; documents worst-case CPU raster only |
| **Budget headroom** | — | **1.853** | **1.82** | `2.0 − t_advance` ms left for GPU Rive Renderer on reference Android |

**Justification:** Strategy **A** is accepted because measured advance alone is **7.4%** of the 2 ms frame budget, leaving **≥ 1.82 ms** for GPU Rive Renderer draw on the reference device. Software-GL render time is excluded from the acceptance math because Flutter release builds on Android/iOS use **Impeller + Rive Renderer**, not CLI software rasterisation.

**Formal total `t_avatar` on reference hardware** (Helio G85–class, Impeller on, one visible Character) is recorded by **P11-047** (`integration_test/avatars_perf_test.dart`). Until P11-047 passes, OW-002 stays open but **does not block** this renderer choice.

## Decision

1. **Ship Rive Renderer (strategy A)** via `RiveNative.init()` in `main.dart`, one `RiveWidgetController` per visible character, `AvatarDirector` writes CharacterVM only (ADR-030).
2. **Do not** implement strategy B or legacy `avatars/*` SMInput engines for new screens.
3. **Offscreen:** pause controller when not visible; long lists use `CharacterChip` artboard (same VM instance).
4. **Over-budget mitigation (P11-047):** if measured `t_avatar` > 2 ms on reference device, degrade to chip-only in scroll-heavy surfaces before dropping lip-sync fidelity.

## Consequences

- P11-035 codegen and contract tests target Rive Renderer bindings.
- P11-047 enforces ≤ 300 KB and records per-artboard draw metrics against this table.
- Lip-sync consumes ADR-033 sidecars; no client-side aligner keys.

## Alternatives considered

- **Strategy B (Impeller replay)** — Rejected; violates single `.riv` source (§4.6 step 7) and exceeds draw-call budget with nested Hair/Headwear artboards.
- **Strategy A + software GL in production** — Rejected; 4.2 ms mean render fails budget by construction.
